## Massive Attack vs Portishead - Teardrop on Roads (Jaya Prime Mashup)

With more than 100 million plays across SoundCloud, YouTube, and the wilder fringes of the web, it goes without saying that my most popular and widespread creation is the mashup between these two iconic songs.

But this... this didn't begin with me. Nor will it end with me.

I introduced my brother Zero to "Teardrop" by Massive Attack. He fired right back by introducing me to "Roads" by Portishead. It was only one small part of the story that brought the two of us together. Fitting, then, that on the night I first cut a production-level mix of "Roads" dovetailed out of "Teardrop," he was one of the few present to hear it.

I'll never forget his face.

### The Mashup That Could've Been

Mashups aren't my specialty. Before this, I'd only ever done two of 'em. So, I made a rough draft and sent messages to both The Kleptones and Kraddy to see if they'd be interested in taking the helm on a proper mix. I even messaged Massive Attack and Portishead with that rough draft, asking if anything was already in the works -- hopeful I'd get a "yes" from the masters themselves.

The only one to get back to me was DJ Eric Kleptone. He told me, "You've got this!" ...and linked me to a clean download of Elizabeth Fraser's vocals.

_Sure... I got this._

Two weeks. That's how long I wrestled with the raw, pained vocals of Beth Gibbons (Portishead) and Liz Fraser's heartbreak over losing Jeff Buckley to the waters. If anything, it was purely my love for the two songs that kept the engines running. Even at the bitter end, if Daniel Foland -- good ole BMFD -- hadn't stepped in to help master it, the levels would've been an absolute trainwreck. So many things could've gone wrong. But one thing went flawlessly right: _these songs were born to sing with one another_.

I released the original version on SoundCloud.

### Not the First of Its Kind

This wasn't the first mashup of its kind. Massive Attack and Portishead had made magic like this before! With John Baggott on the Rhodes piano, Adrian Utley pulling out the electronic -- and each of them mainstays across both bands -- then the others on top of the heavy beat and rhythm of Portishead's "Glory Box," Massive Attack's 3D (aka Robert Del Naja) kicked it all off with a version of their song "Risingson." Then, Beth Gibbons joined them on stage to carry it to the finish line with the actual lyrics to "Glory Box" -- to a crowd going absolutely wild. I've queued it up for you here below ([Also on Vimeo](https://vimeo.com/107822578)).

## 2011, January 3: The Viral Age

The difference between "popular" and "viral" is starkly clear to anyone who's survived it. To anyone else? _Potato, pahtahta!_

After EarMilk dropped the mashup during their New Year's Eve festivities, I figured it had peaked. _Pretty cool, nice work, now onto something else._

Welcome to the world of being wrong.

I woke up in the afternoon on January 3 to a tidal wave of messages across SoundCloud, Twitter, Facebook, and my email. My first thought? One of the hackers trying to take down Burn as One (see, "[Others](others)") had finally broken through and slipped past the HYDRA. But when I checked Twitter, the truth was right there... #teardroponroads was trending. My friend Eben was an investor in the platform a few years back. I'd find out later he had no hand in it. Totally innocent.

_I still have my suspicions._

Between the 3rd, 4th, and 5th of January, it reached Number Eight in the World on HypeMachine's Twitter Charts. From there, others started spreading it, cutting their own videos for it, or testing out live mixes just like I had. At least two peeps even tried singing over the track. Listen, when a song hits karaoke levels? It's gone viral forever.

## The Live Cover by Orquesta Sinfónica Corrientes of Argentina

When I got the email inviting me to Argentina for a live symphonic cover of "Teardrop on Roads," I straight-up didn't believe 'em. I'd just finished my largest mural ever in Thailand, "The Heart of the Rose," and while bouncing between Paris and the US, I was throwing shows with Manchurian and Dez whenever we could make it happen.

But something about the invite pulled at me. It brought me back.

The orchestral line-up was attached. Planned events, gatherings, and city guides were all there. It looked undeniably legit. But the invite itself didn't come from anyone actually in the line-up -- that _and_ the fact that I was broke didn't help my odds. I ended up sending a massive "thank you" for the reach-out and said I couldn't make it.

But seriously, you've gotta hear how they brought it to life!

### Extended Listening

For those who've rode with this mashup over the years, expand your repertoire with these:

*   [_Blood of the Moon_](blood-of-the-moon) (The DJ set from 2003 and 2004 that started it all)
*   **Lana del Rey x Portishead** - _Blue Glory Box (Judd3rMan Mashup)_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=IVqVEokuBI8)) (My favorite Portishead mashup)
*   **NIN v Massive Attack** - _I Know You Can Feel Angels (Dreams of Collapse Mashup)_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vOUKpkGxiYc)) (Seriously, don't miss it!)
*   **David Lynch** - _I Know_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wO4YNWr9l8Q)) (Directed by the amazing Wyatt Denny and my favorite modern trip-hop song)
*   **Massive Attack** - _Teardrop_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=u7K72X4eo_s)) (The original classic and its official music video)
*   **Portishead** - _Roads_ ([YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=qj3QPx089g4)) (If you somehow missed it, this is the live performance they played in NYC)
*   [_The Making of a Violent Cyborg Heart_](making-of-a-violent-cyborg-heart) (My follow-up mashup to this one)
*   [_The Passions of Blood, Smoke, & Oil_](the-passions) (My future garage DJ set that taps into this same vibe and emotion)

### 2021, July 7: The Takedown

A year deep into the COVID-19 pandemic, corporations globally started cracking down on any independent creators who even breathed near a trademark or copyright. Both Massive Attack and Portishead had known about the mashup for a decade. While they never responded to my messages, or to the fans, they'd remained silent and let the music live. But the EMI record label finally made their move, issuing takedown orders across SoundCloud, YouTube, and anywhere else it had taken root.

But it was already out there. You can't put the ghost back in the machine.

You can still find remnants of it on YouTube. Here are my top picks for sharing, ranked from absolute favs to meh:

1.  [Ironlake Records](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=lhwhR8mqRUw) (Mashups OG footage from both bands, shown at top of this article)
2.  [Keep Me Chilled](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=fqZ-v4oi2Gc) (Chill, tropical vibe)
3.  [Electronic Mind](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Mg3iMDutWc8) (Features the OG medley of album art I published with the mashup)
4.  [Feik Acct](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Y21iibnltPQ) (Lol, the account name cracks me up, and someone likes grenades)
5.  [Blind Tube Mare](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=NEb-9jtqY_Q) (Slow motion street photography, uncredited)

## With Eternal Gratitude

Shout out in endless gratitude to my brother AychEff Zero for introducing me to "Roads" by Portishead and my sister Gaea Andromeda for introducing me to "Teardrop" by Massive Attack. When the original "haunted" mixes of "Blood of the Moon" were cut, they were among the very first to hear it -- alongside my brother Tristan Skybreak, DJ Ayanami, and Hekate Law.

Massive appreciation for you, Disco Lama. You've always supported the "sad songs" I produce, remix, and mashup. Even when DJing "downer music" got me booted out of Camp PPK that one year at Burning Man, you made sure to get me on top of the Intentheon the very next year -- and specifically requested "Teardrop on Roads." _It means more than you know._

In both gratitude and sadness, to the long-lost EarMilk: You helped elevate so many with your articles and features. I hope everyone who once played a part in building that site has found nothing but their heart's desire in the years since we lost it. It matters.

And, of course, it almost goes without saying... my deepest gratitude to both Portishead and Massive Attack. Your music changed my life forever. I'd go so far as to say your music altered the very course of the world itself. _All of it._

Finally, to you. The one reading this right now. To the fans who -- over the years -- have shared the mix, dropped comments, sent messages, and even texted me when the first episode of _House_ aired just because it opened with "Teardrop." All of you!

_Thank you!_
"We've got a war to fight. Never found our way... Regardless of what they say"
